transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support. My name is Connor. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Connor. I work remotely from home as a senior financial risk auditor, and I am having a severe, debilitating problem with my S-Net broadband. Every time I connect my corporate laptop to my company's Cisco AnyConnect enterprise VPN, the tunnel establishes for about two minutes and then abruptly freezes and disconnects whenever I try to upload large database spreadsheets or open video conference links!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly investigate those VPN tunnel disconnects for you. Before we inspect your router gateway configuration, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 58 St Andrews Crescent, Cardiff, CF10 3DD. And my security question answer is my mother's maiden name, Jenkins.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that verifies the account file. What model is the S-Net Hub?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is the S-Net Hub 5. Connor, I am leading an emergency international audit committee meeting with bank executives in Zurich in thirty minutes! While presenting my quarterly risk balance sheet twenty minutes ago, the VPN dropped out completely, severed my audio, and kicked me out of the boardroom conference! My managing director phoned me in sheer fury demanding to know why my connection keeps collapsing! If I cannot maintain a stable VPN tunnel for this audit, my professional credibility and employment could be terminated! I am in absolute panic!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the acute urgency of leading an international banking audit with Swiss executives in thirty minutes, and having your corporate VPN tunnel freeze and drop during board presentations is an enormous crisis, so let us diagnose the packet transmission parameters on your router immediately to get you stabilized.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much Connor, I really appreciate your understanding of the pressure I am under.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am opening the TR-069 remote management console for your Hub 5 to query the PPPoE gateway encapsulation metrics.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What do the router encapsulation records show?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router WAN interface telemetry shows continuous TCP reset packets and packet fragmentation drops on UDP port 443 and IPsec ESP protocol fifty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does packet fragmentation mean in layman's terms?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your S-Net Hub defaults to standard Ethernet Maximum Transmission Unit of fifteen hundred bytes, but Cisco AnyConnect tunnels add fifty-six bytes of IPsec and SSL encryption overhead.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So when an encrypted packet exceeds fifteen hundred bytes, the network drops it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When corporate packets exceed fifteen hundred bytes with the 'Do Not Fragment' bit enabled by enterprise security policy, intermediate routers silently discard the packets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why standard web browsing works fine, but the corporate VPN dies whenever heavy data is sent!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We will lower the Maximum Transmission Unit size directly inside the Hub 5 web interface.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we adjust that MTU setting on the Hub?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open a web browser on your computer, enter 192.168.1.254 in the address bar, and enter the admin password printed on the plastic pull-out card.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Navigating to 192.168.1.254... entering admin password from the card... I am logged into the S-Net Hub Manager home dashboard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If your corporate IT department doesn't even know how IP packet fragmentation works, they have no business configuring enterprise VPN tunnels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There was absolutely no call for that arrogant and insulting remark! Our IT department manages thousands of corporate users! Please keep your comments professional and help me configure the router!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on Advanced Settings, Broadband, and navigate to the Internet Connection tab.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Advanced Settings... Broadband... Internet Connection. I see the MTU field currently populated with 1500.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Change the MTU numerical value from fifteen hundred down to fourteen hundred and twenty bytes, and click Apply.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing 1420... clicking Apply. Screen says 'Settings updated successfully, re-establishing WAN session'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fourteen hundred and twenty bytes leaves eighty bytes of headroom for IPsec encapsulation headers, eliminating packet fragmentation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me launch Cisco AnyConnect on my corporate laptop right now and test the connection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead, initiate the secure corporate gateway connection.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Connect on Cisco AnyConnect... entering two-factor PIN code... VPN connection established cleanly! Now let me open the large risk spreadsheet from the Zurich server.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Monitor the AnyConnect statistics window to check byte count transmission.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The fifty-megabyte Excel spreadsheet downloaded in three seconds without freezing! I just opened a test video link and it is crystal clear! The tunnel didn't drop at all!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms clamping the Maximum Transmission Unit to fourteen twenty resolved upstream Path MTU Discovery black-holing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What an incredible relief! I can join the executive committee meeting in fifteen minutes with total confidence!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the MSS clamping setting under the router firewall to ensure TCP SYN packets negotiate fourteen hundred bytes automatically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under Firewall, TCP MSS Clamping is currently set to 'Automatic'. Should we keep that enabled?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keeping TCP MSS Clamping on Automatic ensures mobile devices and work laptops inherit optimal segment sizing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will leave MSS Clamping on Automatic.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us check your DNS server configuration to ensure corporate domain name resolution does not experience DNS leak delays.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under DNS Settings, primary DNS is pointing to S-Net default servers and secondary is backup. Does that work well with VPN split-tunneling?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net Anycast recursive DNS servers maintain sub-ten-millisecond lookup times, preventing corporate hostname timeouts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Internal company intranet sites are loading instantly now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check your physical Ethernet cable connection between the laptop dock and the router LAN port.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am plugged directly into LAN port 1 with a Cat6 patch cable. Link speed shows 1000 megabits full duplex.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Gigabit Ethernet provides zero jitter and zero packet loss compared to wireless interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Direct wired connection is definitely best for important financial presentations.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us check the VDSL copper sync line rate on the street cabinet to confirm broadband throughput stability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How is the broadband speed looking on your diagnostic meter?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The copper VDSL line is synchronized at seventy-four megabits downstream and nineteen megabits upstream with clean six-decibel noise margins.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Seventy-four megabits provides plenty of headroom for high-definition video calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Zero uncorrectable Reed-Solomon line errors have been logged over the past twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That confirms the physical line from the exchange is in great shape.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us check the router backup configuration file so you can restore these MTU settings if the Hub ever resets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under System Management, I see 'Export Configuration'. Clicking that... it saved a config backup file to my desktop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That configuration backup preserves your 1420 MTU value and LAN IP static reservations permanently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is very handy in case a firmware update ever resets default settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check your Quality of Service upstream priority settings to ensure VPN traffic takes precedence over smart home devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under QoS Traffic Prioritization, I set my work laptop's MAC address to 'Highest Priority'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Upstream bandwidth queueing will prioritize work packets ahead of domestic streaming traffic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That guarantees smooth audio during peak household internet usage.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to reconfirm, the broadband MTU parameter is clamped to fourteen hundred and twenty bytes under ticket TEC-88190.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, fourteen hundred and twenty bytes, ticket TEC-88190. That is completely correct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will remain the dedicated owner for this support case and monitor your connection profile until the end of the business day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for getting the MTU adjusted so quickly before my audit meeting.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Connor, before we finish, what if my colleague in our Bristol branch has the exact same VPN issue on S-Net? Can he...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tell him to lower his MTU. Thank you for choosing S-Net. Have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Connor, don't hang up... hello? He hung up on me!
